children: , the database and AI-cloud provider, slipped about 1.1% to $138.07 at 11.36am ET time Friday as investors weighed the cost of financing the AI buildout. The stock stood 28.33% below its $192.64 GF Value estimate, a gap that shows how much confidence investors still need before rewarding Oracle's cloud ambitions.

According to Reuters, bond investors demanded an average spread of about 115 basis points from AI-related issuers, versus 78 basis points across the broader investment-grade market. That 37-basis-point gap is an industry figure; it is not Oracle's own borrowing rate. Meanwhile, Oracle reported $19.3 billion in quarterly revenue and more than $30 billion in new AI-cloud contracts, taking its remaining performance obligations to $664 billion.

The orders are real. The harder part is turning them into cash while data centers still need funding. Oracle can narrow that confidence gap by showing how quickly contracts become revenue, how much customers pay upfront and how much financing the buildout requires.

title: Oracle Stock Falls Over 1% as AI Debt Demands a Premium
